dimension_justifications.soundness: The numerical accounting and raw-metadata aggregation are internally consistent and independently replayable, but the central exactness evidence is archived only as runtime booleans and SHA-256 digests, not tensors, and the distributed source ledger is not cryptographically linked to the code-ledger digest recorded by the run. These are substantive provenance gaps for an audit paper, even though the manuscript states the tensor limitation honestly.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The manuscript is unusually explicit about denominators, oracle blind spots, singleton cross-N coverage, and non-claims; all 12 PDF pages are legible and the main text is within the ICLR limit. Verification is nevertheless obstructed by a non-buildable-as-laid-out source snapshot, a stale build record, and absolute source paths in package metadata.
dimension_justifications.contribution: A denominator-aware ownership checklist plus a deeply instrumented single Qwen3.5 reference case is useful, but the contribution remains a narrow self-consistency audit rather than a new mechanism, independent semantic validation, or broadly reproduced systems result. The authors appropriately acknowledge this boundary.

paper_summary: ForkAudit is an executable checklist for auditing full-attention KV ownership alongside recurrent GDN state in a hybrid LLM. The frozen case compares a source-retaining materialization control against a shared-document layout on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, reports cross-layout and cross-fan-out self-consistency from eight PG-19 books, and separates analytic page-pool accounting from absolute PyTorch allocator peaks. It deliberately makes no throughput, scheduler, generalization, or independent semantic-correctness claim.
strongest_verified_contribution: The strongest independently checkable contribution is the raw-metadata-to-summary accounting pipeline: all eight distributed shards pass the supplied replay, the reported 504 request pairs, 4,032 paired steps, 80,640 call records, cross-N coverage, and memory formulas reconstruct, and the three figures plus two tables regenerate byte-for-byte from the anonymous raw package.
strengths: All 67 top-level MANIFEST entries and all 36 anonymous-supplement manifest entries match their recorded SHA-256 values.

Running scripts/generate_paper_artifacts.py over all eight anonymous shards succeeds; the figures and tables are byte-identical to the submission, and the only artifact_metrics difference is its source-digest block after metadata redaction.
The copied governance suite reruns successfully with 17/17 tests, including the advertised serialized-artifact mutation checks.
The paper correctly distinguishes PyTorch allocator peaks from page pools and from unmeasured NVML/process/service capacity.

Sections 5.1 and 6, the supplement README, and Appendix D clearly disclose that logits, KV, and GDN tensors are not archived and that digests/runtime torch.equal flags are not an offline numerical replay.

The citation lock provides primary URLs plus local support/non-support boundaries for every cited key; the reconstructed LaTeX build has no final undefined citations or references and its extracted text matches the submitted PDF.
questions: Can the authors provide a path-normalized, run-bound source ledger whose digest is itself recorded in the raw shards, or provide the original ledger preimage for the recorded 44c3... code-ledger digest after safe anonymization?

Can the exact PG-19 manifest, protocol manifest, model-weight ledger, model revision, and an installable environment/container be distributed so that the provided launcher can run without author-only files?

Can full tensors for a representative stratified subset, or an independent rerun with recomputable tensor artifacts, be released so that exactness is checked from values rather than trusted booleans and digests?

Why does build_record.json name a latest PDF hash/size that differs from manuscript/main.pdf, and can the source package be emitted in directly buildable paths with a build record for the submitted bytes?
Was anonymity scanning applied to the whole review snapshot? The current top-level manifest and package-closure audit disclose a personal home-directory username and absolute project path.

issues.location: Abstract lines 45-49; Section 5.1 lines 374-383; Section 6 Evidence limitations lines 522-529; Appendix D lines 663-669; supplement_anonymous/README.md
issues.observed_evidence: The shards contain generated tokens, per-step logit SHA-256 values, final logical-KV/GDN digests, and author-recorded runtime torch.equal booleans. They do not contain the logit, KV, or GDN tensors. The supplied replay therefore checks equality of already-recorded digests/flags and aggregation, but cannot recalculate tensor equality or the hashes from underlying numerical values.
issues.why_it_matters: Exact runtime equality is the central empirical result. The package strongly records what the runner said, but an independent reviewer cannot distinguish a correct GPU comparison from an erroneous or incorrectly serialized comparison without rerunning the unavailable environment or inspecting archived values. This limits the result to provenance-backed self-report rather than independently recomputable numerical evidence.
issues.required_fix: Archive full tensors for a representative, preregistered coverage set (and all mismatch-sensitive state where feasible), or provide a complete independently executable rerun package and an offline verifier that recomputes tensor hashes and torch.equal results from values. Keep the current bounded wording.
issues.verification_test: Starting from distributed tensor values or a clean rerun, independently recompute every selected logit/KV/GDN digest and equality relation, then compare the recomputed records with the archived shard and aggregate values without consulting stored pass booleans.
issues.evidence_needed: Archived numerical tensors with shapes/dtypes/ordering and an offline verifier, or a successful independent GPU rerun from a complete public environment and input manifest.

issues.location: supplement_anonymous/raw_primary/static-dry-run.json field code_ledger_sha256; multifork-resident-summary.json frozen_identity; code/EXECUTED_SOURCE_SHA256; provenance/original_evidence_digests.json; Reproducibility Statement lines 547-558
issues.observed_evidence: Every shard and the aggregate record the executed code-ledger digest 44c3a86a..., but the distributed EXECUTED_SOURCE_SHA256 file hashes to ca96cc2a.... Its per-file values match the copied sources, yet the original path-bearing ledger preimage for 44c3... is absent, and original_evidence_digests.json is a later derivative not bound by the raw run. Thus the package verifies its copied files but does not independently link those bytes to the execution identity recorded by the shards.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper's distinctive claim is an execution-provenance audit. A broken run-to-source commitment leaves open whether the distributed implementation is exactly what produced the archived measurements, even though its internal hashes are consistent.
issues.required_fix: Use a path-independent canonical source manifest at execution time and record its digest in every shard, or publish a safely anonymized preimage for the existing 44c3... digest together with a deterministic verification procedure that maps each executed entry to the distributed file.
issues.verification_test: A reviewer computes one canonical ledger directly from the distributed source closure and obtains exactly the code-ledger digest embedded in static-dry-run, all eight shards, and the aggregate summary.
issues.evidence_needed: The run-bound canonical ledger/preimage and deterministic path-normalization or mapping rules.

issues.evidence_needed: Missing manifest/ledger files, exact model/data provenance, environment lock/container, and an end-to-end reproduction transcript.

ethics_concerns: I found no human-subject or dataset-ethics concern within the paper's stated scope, but the double-blind review package leaks a personal local username and absolute home/project path in top-level provenance metadata. This is a concrete privacy and anonymity concern that should be removed before submission.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by an isolated AI subagent for internal pre-submission quality control. It inspected only the frozen round-1 submission snapshot and the supplied ICLR rubric/protocol, and did not inspect prior reviews, author plans, score targets, or the parent workspace.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A clean, fully anonymized, directly buildable snapshot with a build record matching the exact submitted source and PDF bytes.
A run-bound canonical source manifest whose digest recomputes from the distributed executed source closure.
All launcher-required input ledgers plus an exact model revision, environment lock/container, and successful clean-machine reproduction transcript.
Archived tensors for a meaningful coverage set or an independent GPU rerun that recomputes tensor equality and all archived digests from values.
For a score above 6, broader evidence or an independent semantic oracle that materially extends the current single-case self-consistency result.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Any failure to reproduce the current aggregate, capacity arithmetic, or call cardinalities from the eight shards.
A mismatch between archived runtime equality flags and equality recomputed from released tensors or an independent rerun.
Evidence that the distributed source differs from the code actually executed, or that the redaction changed scientific numeric/boolean fields.
Failure of a primary citation's metadata or local support claim after external revalidation.
Additional unredacted identifiers or private infrastructure metadata elsewhere in the final submission package.
review_limitations: I could not rerun the full eight-GPU Qwen3.5 experiment because model weights, PG-19 text, required input ledgers, the frozen environment, and H20 hardware are not contained in the snapshot.
Under the blind-snapshot constraint I assessed citation provenance from the supplied lock and bibliography but did not browse external sources to revalidate every metadata field.
I did not manually read every byte of the approximately 236 MB shard corpus; I validated every file hash and ran the supplied derivation across all eight parsed shards.
The successful LaTeX rebuild required staging the oddly nested snapshot files into their referenced relative paths; I did not alter the frozen submission.
